text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Debt burden is next Liberal target: Once the deficit is gone, additional spending will go toward encouraging growth, Martin says.
- Child poverty leaves Canadians divided on blame: Government surveys find shame, no unanimity on how to combat it.
- Compromise ends bickering between France, Germany: Unemployment problem gains recognition at EU summit.
- B.C. cracks down on cigarette makers: Tobacco industry calls plan a tax grab.
- Child-care plan makes Quebec distinct: An ambitious, European-style social program provides cradle-to-grade-school subsidies for all families, rich and poor.
- CP sells stake in Laidlaw: Billion-dollar transaction with brokers part of strategy to concentrate on core investments.
- Group takes control of Kmart Canada: Quebec pension fund, U.S. investors buy stake for C$185 million, install Bata executive as president.
- Laurentian mulls changes to its ownership: Selling all shares to outsider an option.
- Celestica to buy HP plant in 3rd acquisition this year: Onex unit to purchase workstation assembly operation.
- Group buys Kmart Canada: Analysts skeptical 123-store chain will remain intact and see C$185-million deal as precursor to its breakup.
